name: Giants’ Dance

attributes.attribute: is called Giant's Dance in legend
is named Côr y Cewri or Llam y Cewri in Welsh
means the giants' ring-dance in Latin
attributed the name Giant's Dance to Stonehenge

sources: Grinsell, Leslie V. Folklore of Prehistoric Sites in Britain. London: David & Charles, 1976, 28.
Spence, Lewis. The Minor Traditions of British Mythology. (New York: Benjamin Blom, Inc., 1972), 84.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Giant's Dance is the legendary name that Geoffrey of Monmouth gave to Stonehenge. In his history he wrote that Merlin brought the stones from Ireland. Welsh accounts call the monument Côr y Cewri or Llam y Cewri.

okr.objective: Document Giant's Dance as the legendary Welsh and Latin name for Stonehenge.
key_results: Attribute the name Giant's Dance to Geoffrey of Monmouth
Record the Irish origin of the stones in his account
Give the Welsh names Côr y Cewri and Llam y Cewri
okr.evidence: Koch, The Encyclopedia of Celtic Culture, 2006
